description:
How to write LinkedIn hooks that actually work, based on 131 viral examples from 21 creators.

LinkedIn's algorithm reads your first 40 to 50 words before it decides whether to distribute your post. That window is your hook, and it works on two audiences at once: the human deciding whether to tap "see more," and the 360Brew model deciding whether your post gets reach at all. 

These 5 hook formats (Dense, Punchy + Context, Single-Line Bomb, Stacked, and Hybrid) open a curiosity gap that earns both. I also break down why LinkedIn renders by pixel width, not character count, so your hook actually fits above the fold on mobile.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN:
 Why LinkedIn judges your post on the first 40 to 50 words
 The 5 hook formats working across SaaS, agency, ecom, B2B, content, and AI
 Why pixel width beats character count, and the real mobile line budget
 How to write a Dense hook that fits roughly 3 mobile lines
 When to risk the Single-Line Bomb and how to set up the line breaks
 How Stacked hooks use parallel structure to pull the click
 How top creators mix formats once they know the rules
 A free Claude skill that writes hooks in all 4 core formats

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 A hook is an algorithmic signal, not just emotional bait
 LinkedIn renders hooks by pixel width, around 110 width units per line on mobile
 The Punchy + Context format has the highest hit rate of the five
 The Single-Line Bomb is the highest-variance hook and the easiest to break
 Every format works by opening a gap between expectation and claim
 The format is packaging; the curiosity gap is the engine
